newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mondi says five-week strike over.
newsitem.headline: Mondi says five-week strike over.

text.p: Mondi Papers, a unit of Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd, said on Friday a five-week strike by workers had ended after they accepted a pay rise of nine percent and a marginal increase in shift allowance.
The legal strike at the group's Merebank mill was called by the Paper, Printing, Wood and Allied Workers' Union (PPWAWU) to push for wage increases in excess of management's nine percent offer.

"The eventual settlement was very much in line with earlier settlements agreed with PPWAWU under the CCMA (Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration) at three other manufacturing divisions within the Mondi group," the company said in a statement.
It said PPWAWU members were due to return to work at the Merebank Mill on Monday following the agreement.
Mondi said 770 of the 1,320 employees had remained at work. The mill maintained production on all five machines and the supply of paper to customers was "hardly affected", it said.
